title: Theo and the Postcards
premise: Elodie Sterling, a translator whose childhood language is slipping away word by word, learns that the house where she was raised — sold years ago after her mother's death — is going to auction. Sorting through a box of postcards sent by the house's new owner, Theo, she discovers her mother had been writing to him for years, and that the inheritance Elodie believed was lost was quietly given away. As the auction date approaches, Elodie must decide whether to fight for the house or forgive the stranger in the photographs who took it. In the end, she lets the house go but claims the letters and the truth of her mother's love, finding a found family with Theo and his granddaughter.
about_author: Petra Thackeray is a former estate auctioneer turned novelist who writes about the objects families leave behind. She lives in a converted coach house on the coast, where she collects unsent letters at flea markets.

chapters.title: The Tenant Tongue
chapters.summary: Elodie translates a novel in her fading childhood language, reaching for words that no longer come. Her flat feels borrowed; even her memories feel secondhand. A letter arrives: the house on Marrow Lane is going to auction. POV Elodie. Beat: quiet dislocation, the first crack in her numbness.

chapters.title: Marrow Lane
chapters.summary: Elodie visits the old house before the viewing, standing outside like a stranger. The current owner, an elderly man named Theo Marsh, catches her at the gate and, instead of turning her away, invites her in for tea. POV Elodie. Beat: wary curiosity; the past made physical again.

chapters.title: The Stranger in the Photographs
chapters.summary: Inside, Elodie sees framed photographs of her mother laughing in the garden — with Theo beside her. She realizes this man knew her mother intimately during the years Elodie thought her mother was alone. POV Elodie. Beat: betrayal surfacing beneath polite tea.

chapters.title: Auction Notice
chapters.summary: Theo explains the sale: his health is failing, his granddaughter wants him nearer to care, and the house must go under the hammer in six weeks. He offers Elodie first refusal — at full market price. POV Elodie. Beat: indignation disguised as composure.

chapters.title: Borrowed Words
chapters.summary: Back home, Elodie works on her translation and notices how many words she now reaches for in English instead. Her editor warns the manuscript is losing its music. POV Elodie. Beat: grief for the language mirroring grief for her mother.

chapters.title: The Postcards Begin
chapters.summary: Theo sends Elodie the first of several postcards her mother wrote to him over fifteen years, saying she should have them before deciding anything. The handwriting undoes her. POV Elodie. Beat: longing and anger braided together.

chapters.title: What the Neighbors Saw
chapters.summary: Elodie tracks down Mrs. Okafor, an old neighbor, who confirms her mother and Theo were close — closer than friends, some said — in the years after Elodie left home. POV Elodie. Beat: the mother she knew becomes a stranger.

chapters.title: Theo's Side
chapters.summary: In a rare shift, the narrative enters Theo's memory: meeting Elodie's mother at a language class, the slow companionship, his promise never to tell Elodie what her mother asked him to keep secret. POV Theo. Beat: tenderness shadowed by guilt.

chapters.title: The Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Nadia, Theo's estranged granddaughter, arrives to manage the sale and views Elodie as an obstacle or worse, a swindler preying on an old man. The two women circle each other coldly. POV alternating. Beat: rivalry seeded; two inheritances in conflict.

chapters.title: Postcard Seven
chapters.summary: A postcard reveals her mother's illness and a request: that Theo keep the house safe until Elodie came back for it. But the will said otherwise. Elodie confronts Theo, who admits he bought the house from the estate legally — and cheaply. POV Elodie. Beat: fury; the ground shifts.

chapters.title: The Missing Year
chapters.summary: Digging into records, Elodie finds her mother sold the house willingly a year before death — to pay debts Elodie never knew existed. The betrayal she imagined may not be the one that happened. POV Elodie. Beat: vertigo; certainty dissolving.

chapters.title: Nadia's Discovery
chapters.summary: Nadia, sorting Theo's papers, finds evidence he has been secretly sending money to cover Elodie's mother's debts all these years — and hiding it from everyone. She must choose whether to use it against Elodie or give it up. POV Nadia. Beat: conscience versus resentment.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Garden
chapters.summary: Elodie returns uninvited; Theo, frail, finally tells the whole story in the garden her mother loved: the love affair, the promise, the shame. Elodie walks out without forgiving him. POV Elodie. Beat: raw climax of truth-telling, forgiveness withheld.

chapters.title: Translation Breaks Down
chapters.summary: Elodie abandons her manuscript mid-sentence, unable to find the word for 'home' in her mother tongue. Her editor gives her an ultimatum. POV Elodie. Beat: collapse; the outer loss mirrors the inner one.

chapters.title: The Auction Preview
chapters.summary: At the public preview, strangers appraise her childhood room by room. Nadia watches Elodie touch the banister and softens despite herself. Bids are registered; a developer looms. POV alternating. Beat: dread rising; the clock audible now.

chapters.title: Theo Hospitalized
chapters.summary: Theo collapses days before the auction. From his hospital bed he asks Nadia to postpone the sale, and asks to see Elodie. Nadia, torn, makes the call. POV Nadia. Beat: mercy chosen over strategy.

chapters.title: The Last Postcard
chapters.summary: Theo gives Elodie the final postcard, written by her mother in her last weeks: not instructions about the house, but a plea that Elodie learn to be loved by people who stayed. Elodie reads it aloud in her mother tongue — and the words come. POV Elodie. Beat: the language returns; grief transmuted.

chapters.title: Under the Hammer
chapters.summary: The auction proceeds anyway — Theo insists. Elodie attends, prepared to lose. When bidding stalls below reserve, Nadia withdraws as executor, voiding the sale, and offers Elodie the house at the reserve price she cannot afford. POV alternating. Beat: crisis at its sharpest.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Owned
chapters.summary: Elodie declines the house. Instead she proposes Theo live out his days there with Nadia, with Elodie renting the upstairs rooms — three strangers becoming household. Theo laughs for the first time in chapters. POV Elodie. Beat: surrender that feels like winning.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Photograph
chapters.summary: Elodie places a photograph of her mother and Theo side by side with one of herself and her mother, on the mantel of a house that is no longer hers and somehow is. She finishes the translation. POV Elodie. Beat: reconciliation completed in small domestic gestures.

chapters.title: Household
chapters.summary: Winter settles in. Theo teaches Nadia to bake bread; Elodie reads her published translation aloud in the evenings, the old language filling the rooms. The found family takes shape in routine. POV rotating among the three. Beat: warmth earned, not given.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Spring. After Theo's peaceful death, Elodie and Nadia find one last unsent letter addressed to both of them, thanking them for staying. They bury it in the garden and plant something over it. POV Elodie. Beat: inheritance redefined — not property, but presence.
